Law Passed: Alaska HB 25 (polystyrene foam foodware ban) passed both chambers with bipartisan support but was vetoed by Governor Dunleavy on June 25, 2026. No EPR packaging legislation has been introduced or passed in Alaska.
Status Detail: HB 25, which would have banned restaurants and state agencies from using single-use polystyrene foam foodware beginning January 1, 2027, passed the Alaska Senate on May 18, 2026, and the House earlier that spring, then was vetoed by Governor Mike Dunleavy on June 25, 2026. The governor cited economic burdens on small businesses and an unrealistic implementation timeline. The bill did not reach the 40-vote threshold needed for a legislative override. No EPR packaging bill—covering any packaging material including bags, film, or other formats—has been introduced in Alaska in the current or recent legislative sessions.

Law Passed: California SB 54 (Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act, enacted June 2022) has finalized implementing regulations effective May 1, 2026, and is now in active implementation with multiple legal challenges pending.
Status Detail: Final permanent regulations were approved by the California Office of Administrative Law on May 1, 2026 and took effect immediately, triggering a June 1, 2026 producer registration deadline with CAA or CalRecycle. CAA submitted its inaugural California EPR Program Plan to the Advisory Board on June 15, 2026, opening a public comment period through August 14, 2026. Two separate lawsuits challenging the regulations were filed in June 2026 — one by environmental groups in California state court on June 2, and a federal constitutional challenge by a coalition of 17 state attorneys general and the National Association of Wholesaler-Distributors on June 22 — but the regulations remain in effect and CalRecycle and CAA are proceeding with implementation toward a full program launch by January 1, 2027.

Law Passed: No packaging EPR law has passed in Connecticut. Two bills attempted in the 2025 and 2026 sessions both failed: HB 6917 (2025 session, packaging-EPR feasibility study) died after being tabled on the Senate calendar on June 4, 2025, and HB 5151 (2026 session, EPR recommendations based on waste characterization study) died in committee when the 2026 legislative session ended.
Status Detail: Connecticut has no enacted packaging EPR law and no active packaging EPR bill. HB 6917, introduced in the 2025 session to mandate a study on the need and viability of packaging EPR by January 15, 2027, passed the House but died on the Senate calendar. Law Passed: Maine's foundational packaging EPR law (LD 1541, signed July 2021) is in active implementation. An amending law (LD 1423, signed June 20, 2025) updated definitions and aligned the program with other state EPR frameworks. The program rule (Chapter 428) was amended in March 2026 to add the Packaging Material Types List (Appendix A). On June 15, 2026, Maine DEP issued an RFP for a Stewardship Organization — a critical milestone that had been repeatedly delayed. The program currently covers all consumer packaging material types regardless of material, including plastic film, poly bags, paper, and other bagging formats used in packaging.
Status Detail: Maine DEP issued the Stewardship Organization RFP on June 15, 2026, marking the start of Step 4 ('Contracting an SO') of the nine-step implementation process. The SO selection and contracting timeline has shifted; DEP now anticipates producer registration and invoicing will begin at the end of 2026, with municipal reimbursements expected to begin at the end of 2027. The earlier May 2026 producer registration deadline has been superseded by this revised schedule.

Law Passed: Maryland SB 901 (Packaging and Paper Products Producer Responsibility Plans Act) was signed into law on May 13, 2025. Implementing regulations adopted by MDE on May 5, 2026 became effective May 25, 2026. Covered materials include primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging of all material types (plastic film, paper, metal, glass), plus service packaging such as carry-out bags and bulk goods bags.
Status Detail: MDE adopted its first set of implementing regulations on May 5, 2026, published in the Maryland Register on May 15, 2026, and effective May 25, 2026; these regulations focus on the registration process. The Circular Action Alliance (CAA) is the sole approved PRO; producers were required to register and submit a simplified supply report to CAA by May 31, 2026, and the PRO must file a registration form with MDE by July 1, 2026. MDE has indicated additional rulemakings will follow, with a full Producer Responsibility Plan due October 1, 2028.

Law Passed: New Hampshire HB 1789-FN (2026), an EPR packaging bill introduced January 7, 2026, was killed on February 19, 2026 via a House vote adopting a motion to deem it 'Inexpedient to Legislate.' No EPR packaging law has passed in New Hampshire.
Status Detail: HB 1789-FN was introduced to the New Hampshire House of Representatives on January 7, 2026, and would have established a packaging reduction program requiring producers selling or distributing products in packaging to pay stewardship fees based on quantity and type of packaging — covering all packaging types including plastic, film, paper, and similar materials. On February 19, 2026, the House adopted a motion deeming the bill 'Inexpedient to Legislate,' formally ending its progress for the current session. No successor bill or reintroduction has been identified as of the current date.

Law Passed: New Jersey Packaging and Paper Product Stewardship Act (S673 / A3744) — re-filed in both chambers on January 13, 2026, after prior-session bills (S3398, S208) expired at the end of the 2024–2025 legislative session; no law enacted as of August 2026.
Status Detail: The bill, which covers primary, secondary, and tertiary packaging including paper and plastic, was advanced through the Senate Environment and Energy Committee in February 2025 under its prior number (S3398) and re-filed as S673/A3744 at the start of the new legislative session on January 13, 2026. New Jersey is one of only two states whose packaging EPR bills carry over from 2026 into 2027, meaning the legislation remains active but has not yet passed. No comprehensive packaging EPR law has been enacted in New Jersey as of June–August 2026.

Law Passed: New York Packaging Reduction and Recycling Infrastructure Act (PRRIA), SB S1464A / AB A1749A, failed to pass in the 2026 legislative session. The legislature adjourned in early June 2026 without the Assembly voting on the bill. The bill remains pending and not enacted.
Status Detail: The New York legislature adjourned in June 2026 without passing PRRIA (S1464A / A1749A), marking the third consecutive session in which the bill cleared the Senate but stalled in the Assembly. Prior to adjournment, sponsors Sen. Pete Harckham and Assemblymember Deborah Glick introduced nearly 150 amendments to the bill in late April 2026, aligning definitions and timelines with Minnesota and California EPR frameworks, removing five toxic substances from the bill's toxics provisions, and updating post-consumer recycled content requirements. The bill covers all packaging materials—including plastic film, bags, and other formats—and would require producers with over $5 million in annual revenue and more than 2 tons of annual packaging waste to reduce packaging by 10% within three years and 30% within 12 years.

Law Passed: North Carolina HB 882, 'Break Free From Plastic & Forever Chemicals,' introduced April 9, 2025, is pending in the House Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House Committee with no advancement.
Status Detail: HB 882 would establish a packaging EPR framework requiring producers to join a Producer Responsibility Organization, meet recycling-rate and postconsumer-content targets, and ban toxic substances including PFAS and phthalates from all packaging materials (covering plastic film, poly bags, paper, and other non-reusable packaging). The bill was referred to the House Rules Committee on April 10, 2025, where it has stalled. An earlier version of the bill (H 279, 2023 session) died in the same committee.

Law Passed: Oklahoma HB 4068, a packaging environmental claims and recyclability labeling bill introduced in February 2026, stalled in committee and died when the legislature adjourned sine die on May 14, 2026. No EPR packaging law has passed or is currently pending in Oklahoma.
Status Detail: HB 4068 was introduced in the 2nd Session of the 60th Oklahoma Legislature (February 2026) and would have prohibited environmental marketing claims on products and packaging — including recyclability, compostability, carbon neutral, and eco-friendly claims — unless properly substantiated. The bill remained in committee with no formal votes and expired when the legislature adjourned early on May 14, 2026. Oklahoma does not carry over bills between sessions, so HB 4068 would need to be reintroduced in 2027.

Law Passed: H 6207 (amended) signed into law June 30, 2025, mandating a Statewide Implementation Analysis (needs assessment) for packaging/paper EPR and beverage container recycling, with report due December 1, 2026. Separate full EPR bills S2656 and H7910 introduced in 2026 remain in committee and did not advance.
Status Detail: Rhode Island enacted H 6207 (Sub A, paired with S 996 Sub A) on June 30, 2025 — not a full EPR law, but a needs assessment directing the Rhode Island DEM to hire a third-party consultant and assemble an advisory council to study packaging/paper EPR and deposit-return system options across all material types (paper, plastic, metal, glass), with a final report due December 1, 2026. The DEM's Statewide Implementation Analysis (SIA) is actively underway, with advisory council meetings held through at least July 14, 2026. In the 2026 session, full EPR bills S2656 and H7910 were introduced but remained in committee review, with H7910 recommended for further study as of May 27, 2026; Rhode Island is on the watchlist for potential full EPR passage in 2027 or 2028 pending the SIA report.

Law Passed: Tennessee SB0269 / HB0600 (Tennessee Waste to Jobs Act), an EPR packaging bill introduced January 23, 2025, was sidelined in the Senate Energy, Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee in March 2026 and is now dead for the 114th General Assembly session (marked dead April 24, 2026). No EPR packaging law has been enacted in Tennessee.
Status Detail: SB0269, sponsored by Sen. Heidi Campbell and cross-filed as HB0600, failed to advance out of the Tennessee Senate Energy, Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee on March 12, 2026, after facing opposition from groups including Ameripen and bottlers. The bill had been amended earlier in 2026 to add small-business (under $10M revenue) and small-county (under 200,000 residents) opt-outs, and it passed the Senate Government Operations Committee 8-1 before being stopped in the Energy committee. Sponsor Campbell has vowed to reintroduce the bill in 2027 with a more intensive public campaign.

Law Passed: Washington E2SSB 5284 (Recycling Reform Act), signed May 17, 2025, is in active implementation. The July 1, 2026 producer registration deadline with the designated PRO (Circular Action Alliance) has now passed. No amendments, repeals, or new bills have been identified.
Status Detail: E2SSB 5284 (codified as Chapter 70A.208 RCW) covers residential packaging and paper products broadly — including plastic, paper, glass, and metal packaging — and is administered by the Washington Department of Ecology. Circular Action Alliance (CAA) was formally designated as the sole PRO on March 4, 2026. The July 1, 2026 producer registration deadline with CAA has passed; producers who remain unregistered after March 2029 may not introduce covered materials into the state.

Law Passed: Wisconsin companion EPR packaging bills SB 778 and AB 772 were introduced in December 2025 but failed to advance before the legislative session deadline in March 2026; both bills are dead for the current session and would need to be reintroduced in a future session.
Status Detail: SB 778 was introduced December 12, 2025 in the Senate and referred to the Committee on Natural Resources, Veteran and Military Affairs; AB 772 was introduced December 17, 2025 in the Assembly and referred to the Committee on Environment. Both bills would create a packaging reduction and recycling program administered by the Wisconsin DNR via a contracted nonprofit packaging reduction organization (PRO), covering all packaging types and requiring producers to meet escalating recycling and reduction targets. Neither bill advanced out of committee before the 107th Wisconsin Legislature adjourned for legislative activity in February/March 2026, and the bill's Assembly sponsor has acknowledged the bills will not advance this session but intends to reintroduce in a future session.
